TITLE:
THE FIRST CUT

LOGLINE:
An unseen editor transforms a rough first test brief into a live cinematic directive before the system can interrupt.

HOOK:
A cursor becomes a scalpel. Every inline revision sharpens the brief until the screen itself feels ready to explode.

SORA PROMPT — 12 SECONDS:
Create a 12-second cinematic teaser titled “THE FIRST CUT,” a meta-tech thriller about an anonymous creative inspector editing a first test brief live inside a dark production interface. Aesthetic: “Editorial Voltage” — electric cyan, warning amber, graphite black, and flashes of surgical white. Pacing is savage: hard cuts every 0.3–0.6 seconds, tightening into 0.2-second flash-frames at the peak. Needle-drop: clipped industrial pulse, mechanical keyboard percussion, rising sub-bass, and one complete vacuum of silence before the title.

[0:00–0:03 — THE TEST]
Cold open on an extreme macro of a blinking cursor inside a dim interface; hard cut to a gloved hand dragging across a glass trackpad; whip-pan across stacked abstract production panels as a rough block of unreadable placeholder lines rapidly reshapes. Cyan monitor light cuts through smoky darkness, with a single amber warning indicator pulsing in the background.

[0:03–0:07 — INLINE]
The beat drops. Rapid-fire cuts: a cursor inserts a sharp correction; a waveform spikes; a timeline snaps into alignment; the inspector’s reflection appears fragmented across the glass; a red revision marker disappears under one decisive keystroke. Camera pushes laterally across the workstation while the surrounding screens flicker in sync. Each edit triggers a dry click and a brief white flash-frame.

[0:07–0:11 — LIVE]
The interface fills the frame as the final revision locks. Hard match cuts between the cursor, a camera aperture closing, a playback indicator turning bright white, and the inspector’s eye reflected in the screen. The room’s practical lights shut off one by one until only the cursor remains, blinking against black. The industrial pulse cuts out mid-beat.

[0:11–0:12 — TITLE]
Dead silence. The words “THE FIRST CUT” slam onto the center of frame in severe condensed white typography with a brief cyan scanline tear. One sub-bass impact distorts the image; immediate blackout.

Style: Landscape 16:9, aggressive editorial grammar, macro inserts, lateral tracking, whip-pans, hard cuts, and restrained flash-frames; no floating camera, impossible interface movement, or dense unreadable visual clutter. High-contrast graphite grade with cyan shadows, amber practicals, sharp digital highlights, subtle sensor noise, and controlled screen bloom. Wardrobe is limited to a dark technical jacket and black gloves; the physical world must remain a believable compact post-production workstation. Diegetic audio includes key clicks, trackpad taps, relay switches, ventilation hum, and one sub-bass title hit. No exposition cards, no readable interface copy, no dialogue, and no text except the final title.

```text
TITLE:
INSPECTOR

LOGLINE:
A creative director's vision materializes in real-time as a brief mutates live in the code inspector, each keystroke collapsing fiction into being.

HOOK:
What if the act of editing the creative brief *is* the story? Watch a teaser assemble itself—cursor, text, light, and chaos—as the director rewrites reality one line at a time.

SORA PROMPT — 12 SECONDS:
Create a 12-second meta-cinematic teaser for "INSPECTOR," a surreal behind-the-scenes thriller about creative ideation collapsing into visual reality. Aesthetic: "Digital Alchemy"—phosphor green code-glow bleeding into sodium tungsten, chrome UI frames, glitch-shimmer, text becoming flesh. Pacing: relentless and recursive. 0.4–0.6s cuts tightening to 0.2s flash-frames as the brief rewrites itself. Needle-drop: lo-fi IDM with sub-bass pulse, digital chirps, one dead-silence vacuum before title slam.

[0:00–0:03 — Cursor]
Extreme close-up: blinking cursor on black. Text appears in monospace—"A first test brief"—then deletes. Reappears. Deletes again. Handheld micro-jitter. Phosphor glow reflects in unseen eyes.

[0:03–0:07 — Mutation]
Beat drops. Rapid montage: inspector panel expands full-screen. Lines of code cascade. Each keystroke triggers a flash-frame: silhouette of a director, hands on keyboard, face obscured by monitor glare. Match-cuts between text and shadow-figures moving in the background. One slow-mo hero beat: a single word—"EDITED"—blooms in neon green, then shatters.

[0:07–0:11 — Collapse]
Pitched vocal whisper: "the brief rewrites itself—" Whip-pans between code, reflection, and a figure standing in a dark room. Inspector window glitches, multiplies, inverts. Hard cuts at 0.3s intervals. Final flash: the director's face, eyes locked on screen, mouth moving silently.

[0:11–0:12 — Title]
Silence. INSPECTOR slams in sharp sans-serif, chrome-edged, with a sub-bass impact. Blackout.

Style: 1280x720 landscape, anamorphic 2.39:1 crop feel. Practical monitor-light halation, crushed blacks, green-to-amber color grade. Handheld and locked-off alternating. Macro focus-pulls on keyboard. No dialogue except the whispered line. No exposition cards. Text appears only as diegetic code and title. Grain: 16mm digital. Audio texture: mechanical key-clicks layered under the bed, one moment of pure silence before the title hit.
```
